source_text:
Ἑξῆς δὲ περὶ τοῦ μὴ κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ Ἰουδαίοις θεοσεβεῖν αὐτοὺς οἶμαί σε μάλιστα ποθεῖν ἀκοῦσαι.
Ἰουδαῖοι τοίνυν, εἰ μὲν ἀπέχονται ταύτης τῆς προειρημένης λατρείας, καλῶς θεὸν ἕνα τῶν πάντων σέβειν καὶ δεσπότην ἀξιοῦσι φρονεῖν: εἰ δὲ τοῖς προειρημένοις ὁμοιοτρόπως τὴν θρησκείαν προσάγουσιν αὐτῷ ταύτην, διαμαρτάνουσιν.
ἃ γὰρ τοῖς ἀναισθήτοις καὶ κωφοῖς προσφέροντες οἱ Ἕλληνες ἀφροσύνης δεῖγμα παρέχουσι, ταῦθ̓ οὗτοι καθάπερ προσδεομένῳ τῷ θεῷ λογιζόμενοι παρέχειν μωρίαν εἰκὸς μᾶλλον ἡγοῖντ̓ ἄν, οὐ θεοσέβειαν.
ὁ γὰρ ποιήσας τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ πᾶσιν ἡμῖν χορηγῶν, ὧν προσδεόμεθα, οὐδενὸς ἂν αὐτὸς προσδέοιτο τούτων ὧν τοῖς οἰομένοις διδόναι παρέχει αὐτός.
οἱ δέ γε θυσίας αὐτῷ δἰ αἵματος καὶ κνίσης καὶ ὁλοκαυτωμάτων ἐπιτελεῖν οἰόμενοι καὶ ταύταις ταῖς τιμαῖς αὐτὸν γεραίρειν, οὐδέν μοι δοκοῦσι διαφέρειν τῶν εἰς τὰ κωφὰ τὴν αὐτὴν ἐνδεικνυμένων φιλοτιμίαν: τῶν μὲν μὴ δυναμένοις τῆς τιμῆς μεταλαμβάνειν, τῶν δὲ δοκούντων παρέχειν τῷ μηδενὸς προσδεομένῳ.
orientation: The author has just finished refuting pagan idolatry and now turns to the second part of Diognetus's question: whether Christians worship God in the same way as the Jews.
pass_a_gloss: Next, about the fact that they do not worship God in the same way as the Jews, I think you especially desire to hear. The Jews then, if they abstain from this previously mentioned worship, rightly think it proper to revere one God of all things and master; but if they offer this worship to him in the same manner as the previously mentioned things, they go astray. For what the Greeks, offering to the senseless and deaf things, provide as a display of foolishness, these people, reckoning to provide to God as if he were in need, would likely consider rather folly, not piety. For the one who made the heaven and the earth and all things in them and who supplies to all of us the things of which we have need, would himself need none of these things which he himself provides to those who think they are giving. But those who think to perform sacrifices to him through blood and fat and burnt offerings and to honor him with these honors, seem to me to differ in no way from those displaying the same ambition toward the deaf things: the one group cannot share in the honor, the other group thinks to provide it to the one who needs nothing.

choices.why: The glossary gives 'piety' for θεοσέβεια, but here the infinitive is verbal; rendering as 'worship God' keeps the action clear and avoids the banned 'worship of God' as a noun phrase.
The term pairs with 'God' as a title of sovereign authority; 'master' is the plain literal sense and matches the author's emphasis on God's lordship over all.
The context contrasts Jewish sacrificial practice with true piety; 'worship' captures the concrete ritual observance meant here, distinct from the inner disposition of θεοσέβεια.
The author uses this word for the Greeks' display in offering to senseless idols; 'foolishness' is the plain literal sense and parallels μωρίαν later in the sentence.
The author distinguishes this term from ἀφροσύνη; 'folly' keeps the distinction visible while remaining literal.
The word refers to the savor or fat of burnt sacrifice; 'fat' is the concrete literal sense and matches the earlier section's mention of 'blood and fat.'

pass_b_english: Next, I think you are especially eager to hear about why Christians do not worship God in the same way as the Jews.

Now if the Jews abstain from the worship I have just described, they are right to think that they honor one God as master of all things. But if they offer him this same kind of worship in the manner I have described, they are mistaken.
For what the Greeks offer to senseless and deaf idols as a display of foolishness, the Jews offer to God as though he needed it. One would more reasonably consider this folly, not piety.

For the one who made heaven and earth and everything in them, and who supplies all of us with what we need, would himself need none of those things which he supplies to those who think they are giving to him.

And those who think they are performing sacrifices to him with blood and fat and burnt offerings, and honoring him with these rites, seem to me no different from those who show the same devotion to deaf idols. The one group offers to things that cannot receive the honor; the other group thinks it is offering to one who needs nothing.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires the term "piety" for θεοσεβεῖν, not "worship".
last_rejected.ruling: θεοσεβεῖν means 'worship God' or 'be pious'; both are valid. No glossary evidence shown requiring 'piety' exclusively.
